title: Browser navigation policy refusals
pins: Which URLs a browser policy refuses, and under WHICH CODE, in every language. The code is the contract — a consumer switches on it to decide whether to retry, widen a list, or surface a hard stop. The message is deliberately not pinned; the three implementations word these differently on purpose, and a test over the prose holds every language to a translation and reddens on a wording improvement that changed nothing.

ts.gap: url-0005, url-0006 and url-0007 diverge and are recorded as `divergence` rather than skipped. All three languages REFUSE the same URLs — the security behaviour is identical and every private address is blocked — but the reference names the refusal `private_network_refused` and this port names it `private_address_refused`. A consumer switching on the code gets no match. The port also exposes it as `.code` where the reference exposes `.reason`. See G-21.

py.gap: Identical to ts, on the same three rows, with the same code. The two ports agree with each other everywhere — this is one rename made once and mirrored, not two independent drifts. See G-21.
